title: Kernel conductor: lightweight runtime profiler + decision policy for per-request kernel choice
creator: Ava Reynolds
description:
Problem: The runtime currently selects a kernel family at model load or for broad buckets (short/long) which misses per-request opportunities. On heterogenous hardware and with variable sequence-length mixes (chat vs summarization vs embeddings), a static choice causes 5-30% higher p50/p95 token latency and up to 18% cost overhead for some workloads.

Goal: Implement a "kernel conductor" component: a lightweight, low-overhead profiler plus a decision policy that chooses the best kernel variant at runtime per-request or per-mini-batch. The conductor should be sequence-length aware, GPU-architecture aware (A100/H100/RTX/GPU types), and respect latency SLO vs throughput tradeoffs. It must integrate with existing prefill/decode scheduling and KV cache logic so the decision remains consistent across prefill+decode paths.

Scope: prototype an online microbenchmark that runs targeted micro-runs on cold paths, collect a small fingerprint (seqlen distribution, layer shapes, batch size, kv-hit-rate), consult a compact cost table + cached empirical timings, and pick kernel variant (e.g., fused-flash, warp-fused, triton-matmul, fallback reference). Provide a policy DSL for risk profiles (aggressive-cost, latency-safe, throughput-max). Deliver rollout to 10% of traffic behind a feature flag with monitoring and automatic rollback if p99 regresses >5%.
acceptance_criteria: Conductor component implements a <1ms median overhead per request for kernel decision (measured on A100).
Per-request kernel selection reduces p50 token latency by at least 6% and p95 by at least 4% on the combined chat+summarize workload compared to baseline for internal benchmark set.
Integration with prefill/decode: a prefill-run and subsequent decode must use consistent kernel variants unless policy allows dynamic switch with validated warmup.
Edge cases handled: cold-start model loads, KV cache misses, heterogeneous GPU pools (route-to-compatible kernel or fallback).
Feature flag + rollout: support enabling on runtime-1.25 with canary, automatic metric gating, and rollback hook.
tasks: Design compact fingerprint schema for seq-len/batch/kv-hit-rate (Ava)
Implement microbench harness inside runtime for targeted kernel probes (Diego)
Build decision cache + cost-table storage with TTL and eviction (backend)
Expose policy DSL and config in runtime config layer (Config team)
Wire conductor into prefill/decode scheduler with guard rails (Diego + Runtime)
Create benchmarking suite across A100/H100/3090 for internal PRs (Benchmarking)
Add monitoring dashboards: per-kernel latency, decision overhead, rollout metrics (Observability)
Rollout: canary to 10% traffic, validate metrics, expand to 50% then GA (SRE)
Document ops runbook and failure modes (SRE + DevEx)
notes: We must keep fingerprinting samples tiny. Avoid running full model microbench per request — use per-layer cheap probes or cached lookups.
Policy examples: 'latency-safe' pins to proven low-p99 kernels; 'cost-aggressive' prefers lowest-token-cost kernel even if small p95 risk.
Consider using eBPF-like telemetry for kernel timings to minimize instrumentation bias.
Potential quick wins: prefilling with fused-attention for long contexts and switching decode to lower-latency kernel for short decode steps.
comments: 2026-01-25 - Ava Reynolds: Spiked fingerprint schema. Proposed fields: median_seq_len, pct_tokens>512, batch_size, kv_hit_ratio, attention_heads, dtype. Posted draft on Confluence.

2026-02-02 - Diego Martin: Prototype microbench harness implemented. Runs <200us probes for common layer shapes on warm GPU. Initial results show fused-flash best for long-seqlen on H100, but triton wins short-seqlen on A100 for certain matmul sizes.

2026-02-18 - Performance review: Bench suite run across A100/H100/RTX. Identified one pathological shape where kernel switch increases p99 due to cache warmup; added gating rule to avoid flip for same-request prefill+decode unless warmup observed.
2026-03-03 - PM review (Maya Chen): Requested acceptance criteria include rollout gating thresholds and explicit telemetry fields. Added p50/p95 target numbers.
2026-03-10 - SRE (Liam Patel): Dashboard panels created in Grafana. Added canary alert that triggers rollback when p99 regression >5% over 10m window.
2026-03-14 - Diego Martin: Preparing PR for runtime integration (see GitHub PR #rwd/infra/4256). Ready for code review; unit tests and integration smoke tests included.
